figures.finding: A resident pays nothing on the first MUR 500,000 of annual chargeable income, 10% on the next MUR 500,000 and 20% on the rest, plus a 15% fair share contribution on net income above MUR 12 million (income years from 1 July 2025 for three years); dependants' deductions run from MUR 110,000 to 355,000.
figures.applies: Mauritian residents, income years 1 July 2025 - 30 June 2026 and 1 July 2026 - 30 June 2027.

sources.said: Annual Chargeable Income Rate of Income tax First Rs 500,000 0% Next Rs 500,000 10% Remainder 20%

All individuals with a net annual income exceeding MUR 12 million are liable to pay a fair share contribution of 15% on the amount in excess of MUR 12 million, for the three consecutive income years commencing on 1 July 2025.
One dependent: MUR 110,000; • Two dependents: MUR 190,000; • Three dependents: MUR 275,000; and • Four or more dependents: MUR 355,000.

figures.finding: The income year runs 1 July to 30 June; the annual return is due by 15 October after the year ends; income outside PAYE is paid in quarterly instalments.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is from 1 July through 30 June.
Income not subject to PAYE is self-assessed, and the individual must make quarterly tax payments. An annual income tax return must be filed by 15 October following the end of the tax year.

figures.finding: The employer withholds PAYE monthly at the bracket rates and remits it to the MRA every month; pay up to MUR 38,462 a month is not subject to PAYE.

sources.said: Pay As You Earn (PAYE) is a system whereby employers are required to withhold tax from the emoluments of employees chargeable to tax at the time the emoluments are received by or made available to the employees. The tax withheld is then remitted to the Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) every month.
Employees drawing monthly emoluments not exceeding Rs 38,462 are not subject to PAYE

figures.finding: The employer pays 2.5% to the National Solidarity Fund (capped) and the 1.5% HRDC levy on basic salary, and the employee 1% NSF (capped); both also pay the Contribution Sociale Généralisée by uncapped pay brackets.

sources.said: The employer must make pay-related social security contributions equal to 2.5% (for the National Solidarity Fund (NSF)) and 1.5% (for the Human Resource Development Council levy) of the monthly basic salary (the monthly salary is capped for NSF contributions). Contributions to the Contribution Sociale Généralisée (CSG) payable by the employer are based on specific remuneration brackets and are not capped. The employee must make pay-related social security contributions equal to 1% (in respect of the NSF) of the monthly basic salary, subject to a cap.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed only on Mauritius-source income; fees for technical services rendered in Mauritius bear a 10% withholding and royalties paid to non-residents 15%.
figures.applies: Non-residents; whether a performer's fee counts as a technical service fee is not stated.

sources.said: Nonresidents are taxed only on Mauritius-source income.

A 10% withholding tax generally is imposed on technical service fees paid to nonresidents for services rendered in Mauritius unless the fees are specifically exempted or the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty.

figures.finding: Royalties bear a 10% withholding when paid to a resident and 15% when paid to a non-resident.

sources.said: The general rate of withholding tax on royalties paid to nonresidents is 15% unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty. A 10% withholding tax generally applies to royalties paid to residents.

figures.finding: A freelancer registers for VAT above MUR 3 million of turnover; the standard rate is 15%.

sources.said: The standard VAT rate is 15%. Some supplies are zero rated or exempt. Registration: The registration threshold is MUR 3 million.
